News.title: Carpenter who ‘shoved air hose into apprentice’s bum causing insides to explode’ tells murder trial ‘it was just a joke’
News.content:
Next

A CARPENTER who “shoved air hose into his 15-year-old apprentice’s bum causing his insides to explode” has told the court “it was just a joke”.

Habip Aksoy, 20, testified he had not intended to kill Muhammed Kendirci – but to dust off his clothes during work in Bozova, Turkey.



“He was covered in dust. It happened while I was trying to clean it off,” he said.

“We were joking around at the time. I did not intend to kill him. I regret it.”



Muhammed spent five days fighting for his life after high-pressure air was injected into his anus using a compressor, leaving him to collapse to the ground.

The indictment states that his abdomen swelled and he began vomiting, prompting Aksoy and other workers to take him to hospital.

He suffered serious internal organ damage and was admitted to intensive care on November 14, 2025.

Footage filmed before the incident shows Aksoy and Muhammed dancing together at the carpentry workshop.

An unidentified friend first grabbed the victim’s hands before his trousers were forcibly pulled down.

Aksoy reportedly released the footage to support his claim that they were friends and that the fatal incident was a joke gone wrong.



He is being prosecuted for “manslaughter with the possible intent against a child,” and could face spending the rest of his life in jail.

Prosecutor Tugay Bek insisted that Aksoy should have “foreseen that the air tube used as the murder weapon would cause death,” Turkish news website Sendika reported.

He added: “There are no other workers, foremen, or anyone else working in the workshop. There is only an employer and five employees.

“These children do all the work in the workshop. It appears that they did not receive any training on occupational health and safety.”

Muhammed’s mother, Nebihe Kendirci, attended the hearing alongside relatives and lawyers.



Speaking before the proceedings, she rejected descriptions of her son’s death as a joke or an accident.

“We are pursuing justice so that those who took our child from us with a death machine operating at 12 bar receive the punishment they deserve,” the distraught mother said.

“We call on everyone who cares, children’s rights defenders and everyone who believes in justice to join our call.

“Do not remain silent. We will not stop until justice is served.”

News.title: Trump rally shooting survivor Jim Copenhaver dies two years after suffering permanent injuries in Butler tragedy
News.content:
Next

ONE of the two men critically wounded during the 2024 assassination attempt against Donald Trump has died, The U.S. Sun can confirm.

James “Jim” Copenhaver, 76, died after surviving the July 13 shooting at Trump’s campaign rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, according to a source close to his family.



His death was first reported on X by journalist Ken Silva on Thursday.

Silva wrote that Copenhaver, who had become a prominent voice among the survivors of the Butler shooting, had passed away.



“I’ve got very sad news: Jim Copenhaver, who was shot at the Butler Trump rally on July 13, 2024, has died,” Silva wrote.

“I don’t have many details at this point, but it’s no secret that Jim was dealing with permanent injuries from Butler—including having bullet fragments still inside of him. RIP Jim.”



A source further confirmed his death to the U.S. Sun, adding that his grieving family is not yet ready to comment.

The U.S. Sun has also reached out to the Allegheny County Office of the Medical Examiner.

Copenhaver was one of three people shot when gunman Thomas Matthew Crooks opened fire from a rooftop overlooking the rally.

Crooks, 20, was shot dead by a Secret Service counter-sniper moments after the shooting.



The FBI later said he died from a single gunshot wound to the head.

Trump was struck in the ear by a bullet, while 50-year-old rally attendee Corey Comperatore was killed while attending the rally with his family.

Copenhaver and David Dutch were critically wounded and rushed to Allegheny General Hospital in Pittsburgh for treatment.



Copenhaver was 74 at the time and lived in Moon Township, Pennsylvania, about an hour from the Butler County Farm Show grounds where the rally was held.

He had attended the event with his best friend Randy and was standing in the crowd when the gunfire erupted.

Copenhaver later recalled realizing what had happened after seeing part of his sleeve disappear and hearing a sound, before turning to his friend and saying, “I think I was shot.”

He had been shot twice, with one bullet passing through his triceps and another striking his abdomen.

His injuries required extensive treatment and multiple surgeries, with bullet fragments remaining inside his body.



Copenhaver eventually recovered enough to speak publicly about the attack and became critical of the security failures surrounding the rally.

The House of Republicans also released a statement after his death.

“We are deeply saddened by the passing of Jim Copenhaver, who was gravely wounded in the horrific shooting in Butler, Pennsylvania.

“Jim endured unimaginable hardship with strength and perseverance.

“We join his family and loved ones in mourning his loss and praying for them during this difficult time. May he rest in peace.”



In an October 2024 NBC News interview, Copenhaver and Dutch spoke about what they believed were failures by the Secret Service and other agencies responsible for security at the event.

In 2026, Copenhaver joined Dutch in pursuing legal action against the federal government over alleged security failures that they argued allowed the attack to happen.

Copenhaver and his wife Marianne filed their lawsuit on June 1 in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Pennsylvania.

The lawsuit seeks more than $150,000 in damages over alleged security failures surrounding the rally.

Silva reported in June that Copenhaver’s lawsuit detailed the extensive injuries he suffered, including abdominal trauma that required further medical treatment and surgeries.



The lawsuit alleges failures by the Secret Service, including issues surrounding the security of the rooftop where Thomas Crooks opened fire.

The Secret Service has previously acknowledged security breakdowns surrounding the attack, including communication, technology, and human failures.

As of the latest publicly available docket information, there is no response from the federal government listed in Copenhaver’s case.

Before the incident, Copenhaver was a retired Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board employee and had become increasingly involved in local issues in Moon Township.

Copenhaver had at least one son and several grandchildren, according to people who knew him.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

After the shooting, his family thanked the first responders, medics, and hospital staff who treated him and said he was praying for the other victims and for Trump.

Copenhaver said he hoped to eventually return to riding his Harley-Davidson with his best friend Randy.

News.title: Hoarder, 63, ordered to clear ‘eyesore P***head Corner’ scrap heap garden or face hefty fine
News.content:
IN A SCRAP Hoarder, 63, ordered to clear ‘eyesore P***head Corner’ scrap heap garden or face hefty fine







Next

A HOARDER has been ordered to clear his “eyesore” garden – dubbed P***head Corner – or he will face a hefty fine.

Eric Stone, 63, has hit back at council boffins and branded the action a “witch hunt” against him.



The pensioner claims his garden is not full of rubbish despite it being packed with old mobility scooters, scrap metal, vehicle parts, oil drums and other items.

Eric has lived at his bungalow in Pergin Crescent, Poole, Dorset, for 17 years and named his home “P***head Corner”.



But BCP Council has now given him four months to clear the garden after issuing a Section 215 notice.

The notice warns he could face prosecution and a fine if he fails to comply by January 20.



Eric said: “This is a witch hunt. I’m being bullied and ostracised by the council.

“There’s no rubbish here. I have scooters which I repair but they are not going to attract vermin.



“How can you ask someone to remove a wheelbarrow from their own garden or stone slabs?

“The neighbours support me so I don’t know who has complained, but I don’t agree with the council that this is rubbish.

“It’s my house and my garden and I pay full council tax so I should be able to do what I like.”

He added: “I’m not allowed to put up a fence above one metre but even if I could I wouldn’t because I like looking out and people can gaze the other way if they don’t like it.”

One neighbour defended Eric, describing him as “the nicest person around”.



But others have taken to social media to complain about the state of the property.

Julie Yetman said: “I don’t understand why anyone would think that is remotely acceptable.

“It’s an eyesore. Do these people ever consider the other people that live on the street.”



Tia Rendell said: “Hoarding brings in pests such as rats and roaches.

“I suspect the neighbours would like it cleaned up so there aren’t rats in their bins and around their properties.”

Others, however, rallied behind Eric and argued he should be allowed to use his garden as he wishes.

Simon Stewart said: “As long as it’s in their garden and they are paying the council tax it’s got nothing to do with anyone.”

Lisa Schollar said the garden had been in the same state for years but described Eric and his family as “lovely people”.



She said: “I gave them a couple of my old broken mobility scooters.

“I think he gets them going again and then donates them to people who needs them.

“If they own the property, I don’t see what it has to do with the council unless it’s a health hazard.”

BCP Council said the state of the property was harming the appearance of the neighbourhood.

Under the Section 215 notice, Eric must remove oil drums, scrap metal, timber, rubble, plastic sheeting, wheelbarrows and broken or redundant tools.



He must also clear broken, dismantled or unused mobility scooters, scooter parts and canopies.

Vehicle parts including loose wheels, ramps, repair equipment and dismantled components must also go.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Tarpaulins, temporary covers and makeshift shelters used to store the items must be removed.

Any waste and debris left behind once the materials have been cleared must also be disposed of.

News.title: Boy, 15, arrested over ‘explosion’ at public toilets in popular UK seaside town
News.content:
Next

A 15-year-old boy has been arrested after an explosion caused “significant damage” to a public toilet block on Bideford Quay.

Cops said it believed the blast was triggered deliberately using aerosols and flammable materials.



Officers were called at around 4.40pm on Thursday, September 17 following reports of an explosion at the council-owned toilets on the North Devon quay.

The toilet block – open to locals and visitors – had suffered both structural and internal damage.



The teen, 15, was arrested on suspicion of causing an explosion likely to endanger life or injure property.

He has been released on police bail pending further enquiries.

Devon and Cornwall Police said: “We are working closely with our partners at Torridge District Council, who have advised that the toilets will remain closed to the public until they have been made safe.

“Investigating officers would like to thank everyone who has assisted the investigation so far.

“They would like to further appeal to anyone who witnessed the incident, or who was in the area immediately before or after it occurred, to contact us.

“We would also like to hear from anyone who was driving along Bideford Quay at the time and may have relevant dashcam footage.



“Anybody with information is asked to contact 101 or visit our website quoting 50260249993.”

News.title: Paedo, 32, bailed to same flat overlooking playground where he took thousands of pics of kids & used AI to undress them
News.content:
AI HORROR Paedo, 32, bailed to same flat overlooking playground where he took thousands of pics of kids & used AI to undress them







Next

A PAEDOPHILE who used AI to undress children was bailed to his flat overlooking a playground before his conviction, a court heard.

Zafer Dogan, 32, was jailed for two years and four months at Wood Green Crown Court today after pleading guilty to a series of child abuse image offences.



But despite prosecutors attempting on three separate occasions to have him remanded in custody following his guilty pleas, courts repeatedly granted Dogan conditional bail.

This permitted the vile paedo to return at his property in Enfield, north London, which overlooked a children’s playground, while awaiting his sentence.



Police discovered more than 5,000 photographs of unsuspecting women and girls on his mobile phone.

Many of these had been taken directly from his bedroom window, while others captured victims he followed through the local area, including children walking with parents or travelling to and from school.

Dogan used AI to turn 33 pictures of women and two of girls, aged seven and 13, into sexually explicit images, including by removing their clothing.

Judge Alexander Jacobs told him today: “No sentence can give those families back what you stole from them through your depraved actions.”

The majority of those targeted by Dogan remain unidentified, prompting police to appeal for potential victims or parents who may have witnessed him taking photographs to contact authorities.

When officers arrived to arrest him on July 16, Dogan fled and discarded his phone into a neighbour’s garden.



The device, which was located by police dogs, contained a further 1,800 indecent images of children alongside extreme pornographic material depicting bestiality.

He subsequently admitted to nine charges at Highbury Corner Magistrates’ Court on August 6.

These offences included five counts of making indecent images of children, possession of extreme pornography, possession of prohibited images of children, creating a purported intimate image of adults, and obstructing a constable in the execution of their duty.

Cops said that more than 600 of the recovered files fell into the most serious classification, including infants and young children being subjected to rape.

The mother of the 13-year-old victim described feeling as if she had been “punched in the gut” when police officers told her what had happened.



She added: “I’m really worried that my daughter’s photos are online and other paedophiles have them.”

The mother of the seven-year-old victim described feeling “helpless”, adding: “Our lives will never be the same again and I can’t do anything about it all because one man exploited my child.

“How can a court put him back so close to his victims?”

The mother of the seven-year-old said she was “desperately trying to move to protect my children from this monster”, in a statement read by prosecutor Sarah Gabbay.

“It doesn’t seem fair that because he’s a paedophile and chose to exploit my daughter, that my daughter, a victim, has to change everything. How is that fair? She’s done nothing wrong.”



The Met Police said that alongside the CPS, it had opposed Dogan’s bail on three occasions but their attempts were unsuccessful and the offender was allowed to return to his flat.

Detective Chief Inspector Brian Kelleher spoke about the force’s “frustration” at the court’s decision to repeatedly bail Dogan, who had used the AI software to “nudify” images.

The detective said the “whole details” of the case were raised in court, “including the fact that he was being bailed to effectively the area where he had been offending”.

Joseph Carr, defending, apologised to the victims and their families on Dogan’s behalf, saying he wished to convey “the sincerity of his remorse and reassurance” the images he made with AI weren’t shared.

He said Dogan’s family have been served an eviction notice to leave their home of 30 years and are moving out in the coming days.



Metropolitan Police Constable Natalie Scagliarini said: “This is a deeply distressing case. Dogan’s actions were predatory and dangerous.

“He targeted the most innocent of scenes – children playing or out walking with their parents – and manipulated the photos he took in the most sickening way.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The nature of his offending has understandably left those who have learned of it feeling unsettled and violated, not knowing when they might be being watched or photographed and for what purpose.

“We remain committed to protecting women and children and bringing those who seek to exploit them before the courts, and I thank those affected by Dogan’s offending whose bravery and support has helped us to achieve today’s result.”

News.title: Small boat migrant dead after suffering heart attack in water as two die in two days trying to cross Channel
News.content:
SEA TRAGEDY Small boat migrant dead after suffering heart attack in water as two die in two days trying to cross Channel







Next

A MAN has died during an attempt to cross the English Channel, bringing the total number of deaths in the last 48 hours to two.

The tragedy happened earlier today as around 70 people were preparing to make the treacherous journey from the Camiers and Sainte-Cécile area.



Police, alongside a Carbon 62 helicopter-borne medical team, were also deployed to the scene.

When emergency services arrived at the beach, several people were in the water, while the victim – an unnamed man in his 30s – had suffered a heart attack, local media reported.



A second victim, a 29-year-old Somali man, was treated for hypothermia, and was transported by firefighters to the Boulogne-sur-Mer hospital.

“The operational report indicates that a man of approximately 30 years old (nationality unknown) was declared dead by the emergency medical team ,” fire crews said.



At the time, they said that “no further groups of migrants are visible in the water.”

The man’s death comes only 24 hours after another man also died on the beach of Neufchâtel-Hardelot, after an attempt to leave for England.

His lifeless body was found in the sea, near the shore.

AFP journalists were reporting on the departure of groups in small rubber boats when one of them discovered his remains floating in the water.



A record 781 migrants have arrived in the UK in a single day as two boats reached British shores without being intercepted.

Ten boats arrived yesterday alone after making the crossing, suggesting an average of 78 people per boat.

The cumulative number of arrivals by small boats in 2026 now stands at 18,565, according to provisional figures from the Home Office.



This is down 42 per cent on the equivalent point last year, when the total stood at 32,188.

It is also 26 per cent below the figure at this stage in 2024, when the total was 25,165.

A Government spokesperson said: “Our progress this year in tackling small boats is indisputable – with crossings down by 42% and the lowest recorded over the summer months since 2020.

“But this week’s events show that while the peaks we are seeing are far below those of previous years, we need to push further and harder in order to eradicate this vile trade.”

News.title: Trans woman, 31, ‘bit off stepdad’s ears, gouged his eyes and raped him before he plunged from balcony trying to escape’
News.content:
EVIL ATTACK Trans woman, 31, ‘bit off stepdad’s ears, gouged his eyes and raped him before he plunged from balcony trying to escape’







Next

A TRANS woman has been arrested after the suspect’s stepdad was found with his ears bitten off and eyes gouged out.

The 61-year-old victim was allegedly raped during the vicious attack at a flat in Brazil, before plunging off a third-floor balcony as he tried to escape.



Aurora Naomi La Fey, 31, was arrested in the city of Manaus, and claimed to have been suffering hallucinations after smoking cannabis.

The victim remains in a serious condition after surgeons had to remove both of his eyes due to the horrific injuries he suffered.



Detective Cicero Tulio said his face was bitten during the struggle, causing the loss of both ears.

Investigators are now probing whether parts of his ears were swallowed.



Fingers were allegedly pushed into his eye sockets, causing injuries that permanently destroyed his sight.

The victim may have also been sexually assaulted after losing consciousness during the attack, investigators said.

La Fey denied rape during questioning, but police said they are awaiting forensic results to confirm the allegation.

After regaining consciousness, the victim reportedly fled towards the balcony despite being unable to see.



He fell onto the roof of a neighbouring property in Manaus’ Planalto neighbourhood, where firefighters and paramedics rescued him.

Emergency crews rushed him to the city’s Joao Lucio Hospital after the attack at around 1pm on Tuesday.

La Fey told investigators the pair had known each other for around five years.



Resentment had reportedly built up because he did not accept that La Fey was a transgender woman.

The suspect‘s mum also told police that the pair had a difficult relationship, but did not report any previous violence between them.

La Fey allegedly claimed to have smoked “particularly potent” cannabis that morning, claiming it caused hallucinations later in the day.

The suspect admitted to waiting inside the man’s apartment while he was out, police said.

La Fey claimed to have been only wearing a towel when the victim arrived, ambushing him as he entered.



The suspect claimed to not remember the full sequence of events, but recalled biting his face before fleeing after the attack.

Cícero said: “We are dealing with an episode of extreme violence, in which the victim was attacked inside his own home and suffered exceptionally serious injuries.

“The investigation was treated as a priority from the outset, allowing us to identify the suspect and seek a warrant for her detention, which was subsequently granted by the judiciary.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

La Fey could face charges of rape and attempted murder, with alleged aggravating factors including cruelty and circumstances that hindered the victim’s ability to defend himself.

The suspect had been due to appear before a judge for a custody hearing before the attack.

News.title: My life is ruined by traffic & romping guests at glamping site next door… it’s expanding so I’m having to sell up at 90
News.content:
Next

PENSIONERS Yvonne and Brian Saddler lie awake again – the sound of couples romping and boozing late into the night at next door’s glamping site had left them at the end of their tether.

A desperate planning battle followed, as neighbours pleaded with the council not to greenlight expansion plans – and then tragedy struck.



The Sun first spoke to Yvonne and Brian over the summer – and since then Brian passed away aged 91, with his heartbroken wife admitting the glamping battle had perhaps played a part in his declining health.

This week, she’s told us she’s now planning to sell up her “dream home” where she’s lived for more than 30 years.

She put her beloved pile on the market immediately after her neighbour won permission to expand her tourism business at her Welsh farm, Swallows Nest, earlier this month.



To Yvonne’s dismay, despite initially throwing out plans to host more holiday makers, planners unexpectedly gave the green light to put more shepherd’s huts at the farm.

The noise created by sexed-up, boozy glampers was already keeping neighbours awake and ruining their lives.

Yvonne and her late husband, Brian, told Sun previously that they were “delighted and relieved” when planners initially rejected campsite owner Elizabeth Pengelly’s application for more huts and tents alongside her herd of alpacas at her smallholding.

The din from the two shepherd huts then already in use for glamping caused the Saddlers “intolerable stress”, they told us.

Since then, just weeks ago, Brian, 91, suffered a heart attack and died.



Yvonne was reluctant to blame the stress of living immediately next door to the site for his death, but said: “It certainly didn’t help.”

Now, following the council’s decision to allow more huts, Yvonne has decided to sell the home she and her late husband bought for their retirement 32 years ago.

She told us this week: “Enough is enough. I don’t want to live here any longer now permission has been given for more huts and more people coming here to stay.



“It’s already very noisy and it’s been so stressful.

“Now I’m on my own I don’t think I can cope with it so I’ve made the difficult decision to sell up.

“It breaks my heart because Brian and I spent so many wonderful years here.

“We bought it because it was so beautiful and peaceful.

“The only sound we could hear was the birds and it was wonderful.



“But since the glamping started in the field next door it’s been hell. I have no choice but to see and find a flat somewhere in Abergavenny.”

Yvonne is marketing her three bedroom home with a local estate agent for £350,000, she said.

When Ms Pengelly submitted her original plans, she wanted to add more tents at the site.



But Labour councillor Dale Rooke said the tents would also be too close to neighbouring properties, including the Saddlers’ home.

He told planners: “Tents are naturally not soundproofed so any shenanigans going on inside will be heard in the wider vicinity.”

But applicant Ms Pengelly then submitted a new plan to add one more shepherd’s hut and washroom on wheels so they can be stored in winter.

The council previously received a series of objections from neighbours – with some claiming sex noises were keeping them up at night.

At the time, Brian said: “We moved here those years ago because it is so peaceful and beautiful.



“You never used to hear any noise other than the birds singing and it has been glorious, until now.

“Our garden backs onto the field and when people are staying in the shepherd huts, we can hear every word they’re saying – and not all of it is the kind of stuff we want to be listening to.

“There’s often a lot of swearing and drinking going on.”



Retired engineer Brian added: “If they had been granted permission for the camping site, our lives would’ve been an utter misery.

“I don’t want that sort of thing going on next door.”

Also at the time, retired factory worker Yvonne agreed.

She said: “We’ve heard people’s fears about couples getting romantic late at night, but to be honest that wouldn’t affect us because we’re usually in bed by 8 o’clock.

“Our bigger concern was the volume of traffic the site would have generated.



“There’s only a narrow, single lane road running up here and if you’ve got a dozen or so extra vehicles using it night and day, it would have led to a lot of noise and frustrations.

“It just isn’t an appropriate place for a business of this kind.”

Another local resident, who asked not to be named, told us: “We live right next door to this field and we hear everything.

“We hear them shouting and playing loud music, and then we have to put up with the sound of them getting amorous when they go to bed.

“I am no killjoy, but I just don’t want to be living right next door to what sometimes sounds like an orgy.”

News.title: Footage gives sneak glimpse into life at Buckingham Palace in the winter — as all staff get gifts
News.content:
Footage gives sneak glimpse into life at Buckingham Palace in the winter — as all staff get gifts

Buckingham Palace has been at the heart of royal life for nearly 200 years, but much of what happens behind the famous gates remain a mystery - until now

A Year at Buckingham Palace- Winter

Ever wondered what Christmas is really like behind the gates of Buckingham Palace? From sacks of festive cards to a surprising pecking order when it comes to staffs presents, a documentary is set to reveal the secrets of the royal residence's winter tradition.

‌



The new Channel 5 show will take viewers behind the famous palace gates to reveal how the royal household prepares for winter, including the annual diplomatic reception, elaborate decorations and the King's Christmas cards.

‌



But amid the glittering celebrations, A Year at Buckingham Palace: Winter also lifts the lid on a rather intriguing festive tradition, with every member of staff receiving a Christmas gift.

‌



View 3 Images Buckingham Palace's very own post office is flooded with Christmas cards every December (Image: Channel 5)

Hero Brit saved others before he was killed by terrorist's rocket launcher at Mozambique beach hotel READ MORE :

With the preview of the upcoming episode teasing that there may be more to the annual tradition than meets the eye, raising questions about who receives what.

One contributor recalled: "My boss remarked, 'Oh, she did think a lot of you.' Who knew there was a pecking order even in gifts?"

‌



The show shows that as Christmas approaches , the palace's very own post office faces an enormous task as sacks of cards arrive from Commonwealth countries around the world.

View 3 Images Hundreds of staff work behind the scenes to keep Buckingham Palace running throughout the year (Image: Channel 5)

Meanwhile, staff prepare for the annual diplomatic reception, the palace's largest indoor event of the year, while selecting the perfect Christmas tree, decorating the historic State Rooms and planning seasonal menus.

‌



Viewers will also discover how a portrait is chosen for the King's Christmas cards and get a glimpse inside the palace's little-known wine cellar. But life behind the gates doesn't stop when the Royal Family heads to Sandringham for Christmas.

The programme explores how dedicated staff care for the palace's priceless silver, artworks and the King's ceremonial robes, revealing the craftsmanship involved in keeping the historic royal residence in immaculate condition.

The four-part documentary series follows life at Buckingham Palace throughout the seasons, with palace insiders sharing stories about everything from private family gatherings to the meticulous preparations required for major state occasions.

‌



View 3 Images Buckingham Palace's very own post office is flooded with Christmas cards every December (Image: Channel 5)

The previous episode explored the palace's busy summer calendar, including Trooping the Colour, royal garden parties and the King's Birthday Honours. It also took viewers behind the scenes as chefs, gardeners, florists and housekeepers prepared for thousands of guests and more than half a million summer visitors.

Among the revelations were how the palace's bees produce hundreds of jars of honey each year, the secrets behind the perfect royal afternoon tea and how the King's commitment to sustainability influences everything from seasonal menus to the palace's rose garden.

Article continues below

Viewers were also given an insight into how the King's ceremonial horses are prepared for the demanding summer season.

A Year at Buckingham Palace: Winter airs on Channel 5 on Saturday, September 26, at 9.15pm.

News.title: Bristol school locked down as 'man with weapon' seen and armed police scrambled
News.content:
Bristol school locked down as 'man with weapon' seen and armed police scrambled

Pupils at Barton Hill Academy were told to stay on school grounds as armed cops descended on the quiet residential street after reports of a man with a bladed weapon nearby

View 2 Images Police outside the school in Bristol (Image: Paul Gillis/Reach PLC)

Pupils at a Bristol school went into lockdown after armed police were dispatched to a nearby incident involving a man with a bladed weapon.

‌



Avon and Somerset Police said officers were called to Queen Ann Road in the Barton Hill area after a report of a man with a bladed weapon.

‌



Pupils at Barton Hill Academy were told to stay on school grounds as the school was placed briefly into lockdown this afternoon for children's safety, Bristol Live reports.

‌



Pupils have since been released but police remain at the scene currently as the area is being searched. A police drone has been seen flying overhead.

‌

News.title: Brit 'missing in Benidorm with no passport or money' as wife issues urgent plea
News.content:
Brit 'missing in Benidorm with no passport or money' as wife issues urgent plea

Geoff Cumiskey, from Workington, Cumbria, has disappeared in the Spanish holiday resort of Benidorm, according to an urgent appeal from his wife

View 2 Images Geoff Cumiskey has gone missing in Benidorm, his wife says (Image: Jam Press/Nikki Jane)

British man who has vanished in Benidorm without his passport and money, his family say.

‌



Geoff Cumiskey, 58, from Workington, Cumbria, is understood to have missed his flight home from the Spanish holiday hotspot, with his wife Nikki Jane pleading for help.

‌



Nikki reported Geoff as missing on Wednesday. She revealed that her husband has lost his passport and has no luggage or money. Nikki also told the Mirror he was due to fly to Liverpool John Lennon Airport from Alicante.

‌



"He was last seen wearing a white Everton top with 'Geoffers' on the back, navy midlength shorts, light blue adidas shoes, and a blue Benidorm cap," she wrote in an appeal on Facebook. "If you can help please get in touch."

View 2 Images His family said Geoff has no money with him (Image: Jam Press/Nikki Jane)

It is believed he went back to the apartment he was staying in to find his passport and since then, there has been no update from Benidorm – with Nikki now involving the police.

‌



She said local authorities are now liaising with Interpol to try and find him. She is urging expats and Brits living in Spain to come forward with any information they may have.

Nikki said in her appeal: “Reaching out to anyone who may be in Benidorm at the minute, or who knows someone who is there.

"My husband Geoff Cumiskey is alone in Benidorm, has lost his passport, has no luggage, and no money. (...) his phone has died, and we are all worried about him and can’t get in touch with him.

Article continues below

“This has been reported to the police, who are liaising with Interpol to try and locate him. In the meantime, I am hoping that there is someone I know in Benidorm at the moment who may be able to help locate him. If you can help please get in touch.”

Her appeal has been posted on Facebook groups in Spain with several people sharing the information.

The Mirror has contacted the Guardia Civil, Interpol and the Foreign Office for comment.

News.title: Heat pump new Thursday government update on £9,000 scheme for UK households
News.content:
Heat pump new Thursday government update on £9,000 scheme for UK households

The Boiler Upgrade Scheme offers support to eligible property owners in England and Wales

View 3 Images Government help is available on heat pumps - file image (Image: Andrew Aitchison, In Pictures via Getty Images)

Andy Burnham's government has today issued a major update on heat pumps. The Boiler Upgrade Scheme is a grant for households in England and Wales to receive thousands of pounds towards a low carbon heating system for your home.

‌



Data released today that can be seen here reveals that August recorded the highest ever number of heat pump vouchers issued under the Boiler Upgrade Scheme (BUS). The scheme offers grants to incentivise property owners to swap existing fossil fuel heating for more efficient, low carbon heating systems including air source heat pumps, ground source heat pumps and, in limited circumstances, biomass boilers.

‌



Ofgem says you can claim £9,000 off the cost and installation of air-to-water or ground source heat pumps in eligible off-gas grid properties until March 31 2027. Alternatively, you could claim £7,500 off the cost and installation of an air source heat pump; or £7,500 off the cost and installation of a ground source heat pump; or £5,000 off the cost and installation of a biomass boiler.

‌



View 3 Images (Image: Andrew Aitchison, In Pictures via Getty Images)

These grants are designed to help UK property owners in overcoming the upfront expense of fitting a low carbon heating system. Yet the surge in take-up shows many Brits are making the switch to clean energy as the Iran war has driven up bills. There has been roughly a 40% rise in BUS vouchers issued in comparison with the same period in 2025.

Heat pumps are highly efficient electric devices that extract and amplify heat from the outside air or ground into a building, the government has said. They can generate approximately 3 units of heat for every unit of electricity they consume. They can slash a property's energy demand when replacing technologies such as gas boilers.

‌



Minister for Local Energy and Jobs Martin McCluskey said: “People across England and Wales are showing record demand for clean heat as we pass another heat pump milestone. More families than ever are switching from volatile fossil fuels so they can save on bills. We have also increased support from £7,500 to £9,000 to help rural households on heating oil or liquefied petroleum gas make the switch.”

Jess Ralston, Head of Energy at the Energy and Climate Intelligence Unit (ECIU) said in a statement today: "August's record month for heat pumps under the Boiler Upgrade Scheme is another signal that this net zero technology is moving into the mainstream, with people seeing the clean transition as a route to energy independence and more stable bills. If the UK had fewer Liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) and gas boilers, we'd be far less exposed to the international oil and gas price spikes that have repeatedly driven up bills and triggered energy crises.

"For years, boiler industry lobbying helped keep the UK locked into gas heating for longer than necessary, leaving households and the wider economy vulnerable to price shocks. More households in the UK are recognising that electric heat pumps offer a route away from the volatility of oil and gas markets, and other countries are already way ahead on installations."

‌



The scheme can prove invaluable for British homeowners. Matthew Bell told the Energy Saving Trust: "My wife says that it's the first house where she hasn't felt the cold. You feel like you have a level of control over the feel of the house that you never quite got with the gas boiler."

This latest development comes as UK energy costs are being driven up by the conflict in Iran. A deputy governor at the Bank of England has warned that interest rates may need to rise should energy prices remain at their current levels.

View 3 Images An engineer checks data on his phone while installing a heat pump - file image (Image: Bloomberg, Bloomberg via Getty Images)

‌



Clare Lombardelli today said: "The main driver of near-term inflation is developments in global energy prices. The energy shock due to the conflict in the Middle East has already pushed up UK inflation, and we expect it to continue to do so in the coming months. There is significant uncertainty about how the conflict will develop, and so about the evolution of energy prices."

This month marked 200 days since the conflict began. Since then, global oil and gas prices have been turbulent, and in recent days these costs have surged, particularly UK gas prices. The war has driven up energy bills, petrol and diesel prices, and inflation across the UK and beyond, with further increases expected.

Ms Ralston said in a separate statement today: "Gas prices have hit a 4 year high, with petrol and diesel costs already climbing and analysts warning that energy bills could rise again in the new year. It's a stark reminder that conflicts thousands of miles away can still hit households here, especially those already struggling with the cost of living.

‌



"The Energy Crisis Commission has warned that the UK remains 'dangerously underprepared' for future energy shocks. It set out that the clearest way to protect households is to reduce our dependence on volatile oil and gas markets through electrification and renewables.

"More drilling in the North Sea won't bring down bills or reverse the basin's long-term decline. If the UK wants to increase energy security, lower exposure to global crises and so energy price volatility, it will need to accelerate the rollout of heat pumps, electric vehicles, and homegrown wind and solar power."

Eligibility for the Boiler Upgrade Scheme

Installers who are MCS certified can apply for and redeem Boiler Upgrade Scheme vouchers on behalf of property owners. Many energy firms in the UK offer guidance on the scheme, with British Gas, E.ON Next and EDF Energy all having details about it on their websites.

‌



Government guidance shows your property needs to be a residential dwelling or small to medium-sized non-domestic premises located in England or Wales. It must have a valid energy performance certificate.

Biomass boilers qualify only for properties situated in rural areas and without mains gas connection. Heat pumps face neither of these limitations.

You need to be completely replacing an existing fossil fuel system - such as an oil or gas boiler - or an electric heating arrangement like storage or panel heaters. Funding won't be available for replacing current low carbon heating systems.

‌



The government says the installation must not get funding from multiple public funding sources, and you are ineligible if you have already obtained government funding or support for a heat pump or biomass boiler.

However, you are still eligible if you have secured separate funding for energy efficiency improvements including insulation, doors or windows. Newly-built homes and social housing do not qualify for the Boiler Upgrade Scheme, although self-build properties are eligible.

When it comes to possible cost savings from having a heat pump, Mr Bell told the Energy Saving Trust: "We haven't figured out really whether we've seen significant savings yet, but I have no doubt that over the life of the heat pump, we will, particularly if electricity prices come down."

Article continues below

To apply or for further information such as eligibility, visit the dedicated government web page on the subject.

News.title: RAF pilots forced to eject from Hawk moments before fireball explosion will make 'full recovery'
News.content:
RAF pilots forced to eject from Hawk moments before fireball explosion will make 'full recovery'

As a veteran RAF flying insructor and a trainee recover from dramatically ejecting from their stricken fast-jet a major probe is launched and all Hawk planes are grounded

View 4 Images Moments from disaster two RAF pilots eject from Hawk T2 above Anglesey (Image: X)

TWO RAF pilots were still recovering last night from minor injuries after cheating death by ejecting from their military fast-jet.

‌



Sources said it is possible their Hawk T2 aircraft, a training plane, may have been steered away from buildings and aimed at a field as it headed for a crash.

‌



It ran into difficulty, crashing shortly after take-off from RAF Valley in Anglesey on Wednesday.

‌



Both pilots were filmed parachuting back to the ground after ejecting at the same time within seconds from the plane crashing.

One source, familiar with RAF practice, told the Mirror : “The decision to eject was likely taken by a senior instructor who pressed ‘eject’ for both people.

View 4 Images Jet crashes after pilots eject, sparking fireball (Image: John Heyworth)

‌



“The plane hit a field and it is likely whoever took control will have done all they could to void it hitting a building or people.”

Amazing footage showed them rocketing out of their cockpits after pressing ‘eject’ before the plane hit the ground and burst into a fireball.

Gp Capt Gez Currie, Station Commander, told the BBC : "The aircraft would have been aimed in a direction that the pilot believed was open field, in order to avoid built-up areas and anybody on the ground."

‌



The Hawk T2 aircraft had been flying out of the RAF base when it smashed into the ground nearby in Pencarnisiog.

It is believed both pilots, a trainee and a veteran flyer will make a full recovery as the RAF launched a full investigation into the crash.

View 4 Images Jet nose-dives into ground after ejection (Image: X)

‌



The T2 version of the Hawk, which prepares pilots for flying Typhoon jets, is a slightly more sophisticated version of the variant used by the Red Arrows display team.

All flying of the craft, including the Red Arrows has been put on hold pending the investigation into what went wrong.

It is believed the two pilots are still in hospital and are undergoing check-ups.

‌



Gp Capt Currie confirmed that the two people involved are a trainee and an experienced pilot.

Asked what went wrong he said: “It’s far too early to even suggest what has happened in this occasion.

"It was a trainee, with a highly experienced instructor on a routine sortie, across the Anglesey area."

‌



He confirmed that in his 30-year career as an air traffic controller, "this is the first time I've experienced this.”

View 4 Images Pilots shoot into air after ejection (Image: X)

It is not known how the two pilots decided quickly to eject.

‌



Both flyers will have had an ejection lever which they can pull individually, although it is believed the instructor will have been able to eject them both.

The RAF said: “Both pilots are doing well, they are in extremely good spirits and expected to make a full recovery.

"A formal investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident is now under way and, as a precautionary measure, the RAF has temporarily paused Hawk T1 and Hawk T2 flying operations."

Article continues below

It is not known when flying of the Hawks will resume.

News.title: 'I want to freeze my baby daughter's eggs — as she's started puberty at 10 months'
News.content:
'I want to freeze my baby daughter's eggs — as she's started puberty at 10 months'

Sophie Dumas' daughter Sienna has been diagnosed with central precocious puberty (CCP), after a health visitor noticed the baby's breast tissue appeared enlarged

View 5 Images Sophie Dumas was stunned her daughter Sienna was showing signs of puberty (Image: Jam Press)

A mum is considering freezing her baby daughter's eggs after she started puberty at 10 months old.

‌



Sophie Dumas was unaware anything unusual was happening with her daughter Sienna until a health visitor noticed the baby's breast tissue appeared enlarged. The 41-year-old took her daughter to the GP and they were then referred to paediatric endocrinologists who began investigating whether she had precocious puberty.

‌



Following a series of distressing tests, Sienna was diagnosed with central precocious puberty (CCP) - a condition in which the brain begins sending the signals that trigger puberty much earlier than usual. She was just 10 months old at the time.

‌



Speaking from her home in London, Sophie said. "The breast buds weren't something I'd noticed before, and as babies are usually the sort of chubby that makes them that little bit more adorable, and also that she was breastfed, I didn't think anything of her appearance as being out of the ordinary."

View 5 Images Sienna underwent tests after a health visitor noticed something unusual about her (Image: Jam Press)

Health visitor saw change in baby, doctors said it was puberty at 10 months old READ MORE :

The mum added: “The tests she underwent were horrible for all of us. She had what was referred to as Stim tests, which was a term I went on to dread, which involved blood tests to take a baseline to measure the LH level, the hormone that regulates puberty, then injecting her with a synthetic hormone to see how her blood hormones react over a period of different timeframes.

‌



“This meant a whole day in hospital. Sienna became so stressed that she sweated the cannulas out, and one of her veins collapsed.

“They then had to draw her blood via another method from her heels with a pin-prick. It was incredibly distressing."

A few weeks later, the family received the news that Sienna's tests were positive for precocious puberty. Sophie says she’d never heard of the condition and was left desperately researching what this meant for Sienna.

‌



She said: “I found that the lack of knowledge about it very hard, and the only parents I could find to talk to were via Facebook groups for it, but even then, they were parents of seven- to eight-year-olds, so it was never relevant.

View 5 Images Sophie said the tests were "horrible for all of us" (Image: Jam Press)

“It feels very isolating, and I still have so many questions about it, mostly about how I can explain this to Sienna.” Doctors explained that she would need regular injections of a hormone blocker known as a GnRH analogue to suppress the hormones responsible for puberty.

‌



Sienna also underwent an MRI to determine whether there was an underlying cause for her condition. In some cases, central precocious puberty can be linked to abnormalities in the brain. Sophie said the possibility was “terrifying”.

Thankfully, Sienna's MRI was clear, and she was diagnosed with central precocious puberty, which has no known cause in many children and is more common in girls. Without treatment, Sienna, now five, would have progressed through puberty years before her peers.

While the condition is not life-threatening, doctors explained that early puberty can affect final adult height because children initially grow rapidly but their growth plates can mature sooner.

‌



The family has been told that Sienna is likely to remain on the hormone-blocking treatment until she is around 11 or 12, although this will depend on her bone age and how she develops. Sophie is now looking ahead to her daughter's future and is considering whether egg freezing could give Sienna more options when she is older.

View 5 Images Sienna was diagnosed with precocious puberty (Image: Jam Press)

She said: “I’m currently looking into that possibility in case her condition affects her fertility later down the line. When she was diagnosed, I was worried that she may not be able to start a family of her own one day if she wanted to, that the choice may be taken away from her.

‌



“Hopefully, the hormone blockers will prevent this from affecting her fertility.” Sienna’s getting to an age where some of the untreatable symptoms are causing her to deal with spots on her face in the areas that are linked to hormones.

“It’s difficult explaining it to her. There’s been some teasing from her school friends who have said they think she has chickenpox.

“It makes me really sad. No one wants to think of their child being upset, especially when it’s from what someone else has said to them.

‌



“Sienna was confused because she didn’t know how to explain to them that they’re different kinds of spots because she doesn’t even understand it. I told the teacher, who said that she knew they were hormonal spots and that she would reassure Sienna and tell the other children that it’s not their job to play doctor.”

View 5 Images Sophie is determined to let her daughter enjoy being a little girl (Image: Jam Press)

For now, Sophie says she is determined to let her daughter enjoy being a little girl. She added: “My main concerns are that all little girls want to grow up before they should, and the pressures around things like breast size, so I am worried that once Sienna understands what would happen if she were to refuse her treatment early so that she goes through puberty, her mental maturity wouldn’t be ready for all that comes with it.

Article continues below

“Puberty is such an abstract concept for a child, so talking to her about it is complicated for her to understand and also for me to explain. Sienna is still a little girl, obsessed with fairies and Disney princesses, and I’d love to take her to Disneyland next year to keep the magic of childhood alive for as long as possible.

“The only advice I would give to another parent who is concerned about anything, even if they think it makes them look or sound neurotic, is to seek that medical advice and even get second opinions. Our health visitor didn’t even think it would get taken seriously and, without her noticing something I never did, Sienna would not have received treatment as early as she did.”

News.title: How sacrificing part of your salary could boost your pension - and reduce your tax bill
News.content:
How sacrificing part of your salary could boost your pension - and reduce your tax bill

Salary sacrifice is where you agree to exchange part of your gross salary for a non-cash benefit, such as payments into a pension scheme

View 2 Images Salary sacrifice can help increase your pension (Image: PeopleImages via Getty Images)

Salary sacrifice can be an efficient way to boost your pension - and cut your tax bill.

‌



Salary sacrifice is where you agree to exchange part of your gross salary for a non-cash benefit, such as payments into a pension scheme. As your gross salary is lower, it means less of your income is subject to Income Tax and National Insurance - so your tax bill is lower. Your employer also ends up paying less National Insurance.

‌



National Insurance is charged at 8% on earnings between £12,570 and £50,270, dropping to 2% on earnings above that.

‌



Helen Morrissey, head of retirement analysis, Hargreaves Lansdown: “Reducing your income can also be useful in taking your income below various thresholds, which can mean you keep your entitlement to things like Child Benefit. Just check it doesn’t impact other benefits, like maternity or sick pay.”

View 2 Images Salary sacrifice rules are changing from April 2029 (Image: Sasun Bughdaryan via Getty Images)

Watchdog accused of failing to hold water firms to account over pollution breaches READ MORE :

But the rules for salary sacrifice are changing from April 2029. From this date, only the first £2,000 of annual employee pension salary sacrifice will be exempt from National Insurance. This means, salary sacrifice contributions above this amount will be subject to National Insurance, although it will still remain free from Income Tax.

‌



Ms Morrissey added: “You’ve still got more than two and a half years to make the most of the system as it currently stands. And even after these changes, pensions remain a hugely effective way to save for your future.”

Analysis by Hargreaves Lansdown shows someone earning £35,000 a year, who is sacrificing 10% of their salary into a pension, would save £700 a year in Income Tax and £280 in National Insurance.

Someone earning £50,000 per year, sacrificing 10% of salary into pension, would cut their Income Tax bill by £1,000 a year, and £400 in National Insurance.

‌



Most people have an annual allowance of £60,000 for how much they can pay into their pension before they pay tax on the excess amount.

Your allowance might be lower if you have a high income or you have already flexibly accessed your pension pot.

Earlier this year, research from the Standard Life Centre for the Future of Retirement showed two in five (39%) business leaders who currently offer salary sacrifice schemes say they are less likely to provide them in future.

Article continues below

One in ten (11%) employers said at the time that they have already decided to withdraw the scheme completely. However, the Treasury said it does not expect significant numbers of employers to stop offering salary sacrifice.

News.title: Is Prince Harry profiting off his mother's death? Take our poll and have your say
News.content:
Is Prince Harry profiting off his mother's death? Take our poll and have your say

The Duke of Sussex is reportedly in talks to produce a documentary about Princess Diana ahead of the 30th anniversary of her death

View 4 Images Harry with his mother, Princess Diana, in 1995 (Image: Getty Images)

Prince Harry is reportedly in talks to produce a documentary about his late mother, Princess Diana, ahead of the 30th anniversary of her death. The Duke of Sussex is believed to be exploring ways to honour Diana’s legacy “in the most meaningful way”, with sources claiming he has reached out to a number of her friends and relatives to take part in the programme.

‌



A source close to Harry told the Mirror: “The Duke has discussed a number of possible projects to mark the 30th anniversary of his mother Diana, Princess of Wales ’s passing, and is still considering the most meaningful way to honour her legacy.”

‌



View 4 Images Prince Harry is reportedly in talks to produce a story about his late mother

‌



The 30th anniversary of Diana’s death will be marked on August 31 2027, three decades after she was tragically killed in a fatal car crash in a tunnel in Paris. When Diana died, Prince William was 15 years old while Harry was just 12.

Any documentary would be expected to be produced through Harry and his wife Meghan’s company Archewell Productions, which has a first-look deal with Netflix.

Speaking on the Mirror's YouTube show Pod Save The King, the Mirror’s royal editor Russell Myers said Harry’s decision to create such a documentary goes ‘beyond the pale’ and questioned if the Duke ‘has the right’ to mark the poignant anniversary in such a commercial way.

‌



Myers said: “Of course it is the 30th anniversary of her tragic death next year, everybody has been trying to have their say and they will be of course next year. Archewell productions are apparently going to produce it, as they've got this sort of first look deal with Netflix.

“I mean the rest of the things they've been producing haven't done too well. We had the Invictus documentary, we had the Polo documentary that absolutely bombed. And I just think this is beyond the pale for Harry to be saying ‘Well I'm going to do this now’.

‌



Russell questioned: “So, realistically, does Harry have a right to do this? I can tell you now that William will be absolutely furious about it.”

It would not be the first documentary about Diana that Harry has had a hand in, as he and his brother William worked together on two documentaries about their mother to mark the 20th anniversary of her death in 2017.

View 4 Images William and Harry appeared in a documentary about Diana in 2017 (Image: UK Press via Getty Images)

‌



One person believed to not be taking part in the project is Diana’s brother Earl Spencer, who revealed in his new memoir, Swan Song: Diana, My Sister, that he deliberately chose to write a book rather than appear as what he described as a “talking head” in one of the many productions being planned about his sister.

The Earl, whose memoir is published on Tuesday, said he feared documentaries could be driven by a “flawed” agenda set by producers, as he revealed that he had turned down “endless, repeated” requests to appear in documentaries about his sister.

Instead, he said he wanted to “tell things how I remember them” rather than follow “an agenda set by some TV producer I will never meet”.

‌



View 4 Images Next year will mark 30 years since Diana's passing (Image: Tim Graham Photo Library via Getty Images)

Harry has long spoken about keeping his mother’s memory alive. In his memoir Spare, he wrote about the devastating impact of her death and the events surrounding her funeral, including the decision for him and William to walk behind their mother’s coffin.

Speaking to People magazine in 2022, Prince Harry said that he always hoped to make his mother proud. “I certainly hope and believe everything I do makes her proud.

Article continues below

“In the 12 short years I was lucky enough to have with her, I saw and felt the energy and lift she got from helping others, no matter their background, ailment or status. Her life and theirs was better for it, however short theirs or hers was. I honor my mother in everything I do. I am my mother’s son,”

News.title: Crashed RAF jet steered to 'avoid built-up areas' before pilots ejected, commander says
News.content:
An RAF jet was steered to "avoid built-up areas" before two pilots ejected out of the aircraft, an air force commander has said.

Gp Capt Gez Currie, Station Commander, said: "The aircraft would have been aimed in a direction that the pilot believed was open field, in order to avoid built-up areas and anybody on the ground."

The Hawk T2 aircraft had been flying out of the RAF Valley station on Anglesey on Wednesday when it plummeted to the ground in nearby Pencarnisiog, narrowly avoiding homes.

The trainee and an experienced professional, who parachuted out of their plane moments before it crashed, are expected to make a full recovery after they were treated for minor injuries.

Hawk operations have been paused by the RAF as a "precautionary measure" while investigations into the crash are ongoing - the Red Arrows are included in the pause as the aerobatics display team use the T1.

The Ministry of Defence (MoD) confirmed that the squadron of Hawk jets at RAF Leeming, in Yorkshire, has also "paused" flying.

News.title: Man jailed for two years over throwing bottle at Portsmouth migrant protest
News.content:
Judge Daniel Sawyer told Somerville that his sentence would act as a deterrent to others following subsequent protests in the area.

Describing him as a "thug", he told the defendant: "Police officers dedicate their lives to the protection of the public regardless of their own views, the very least they can expect is that those who engage in protests treat them with respect and the courts punish those who assault them."

The court heard Sommerville, from Portsmouth, was among a large group of demonstrators protesting at the arrival of the migrants.

They were brought ashore by the RNLI after being picked up in the Channel. A number of volunteer lifeboat crew members were subject to online abuse following the incident.

Prosecutor Edward Warren said Somerville was part of an "initially peaceful and lawful" gathering of a number of people on Ferry Road.

At shortly before 23:30 BST, he was with a large group of men as they were held up by the police line.

The court was told he was identified in police body-worn video as throwing a small bottle and swearing at police.

When later interviewed by police, he said he had found the bottle on the ground and was going to throw it into a nearby bush, but was angry and so threw it up into the air.

Defence barrister Helen Easterbrook said Somerville had been "caught up" in the disturbances.

She said he had been attempting to be a "calming influence" on the crowd but had thrown the bottle "in frustration".

Four other men are awaiting sentence having also been charged with violent disorder following the protest in Eastney.

News.title: 'It has broken us as a family,' mother of poison seller victim tells hearing
News.content:
The mother of a British victim of poison seller Kenneth Law has said his death and the way that he died had "destroyed" their family.

Tanya Whitaker broke down at the start of her video statement about the death of her son, Samuel, shown on the second day of a four-day sentencing hearing of Law in Ontario, saying: "He barely had a chance."

The University of Warwick student was found collapsed outside his halls after taking poison sold by Law, who has admitted 14 counts of aiding suicide in Canada but has also been linked to nearly 80 deaths in the UK.

Debbie Cornish echoed Whitaker's sentiments, telling the hearing that her family was "still fighting" to stay together years on from her daughter Danielle's death.

A plea deal with Canadian authorities means Law will not face charges in the UK or over any British deaths, but impact statements from their families are being read this week.

"The enormity of losing a child is catastrophic," Whitaker told a Canadian court on Thursday. "Samuel was just 19 when he was handed the tools that ended his precious life."

She continued: "It has broken me completely and utterly. It has broken us as a family and me as a mother.

"Our son died alone at university 100 miles away from his family. We will never be able to forgive ourselves for this happening."

News.title: Ex-England striker Andy Carroll reveals he was sexually assaulted in 2021
News.content:
Former England striker Andy Carroll has revealed he was sexually assaulted by a man in 2021.

The 37-year-old, who was automatically granted anonymity as a victim of sexual assault, has made the details public in an autobiography titled 'Owning it'.

The incident took place at Carroll's home, during his second spell with his hometown club Newcastle and led to the perpetrator being jailed for three years.

Carroll, now a player/co-owner of non-league club Dagenham & Redbridge, says he decided to include the incident in his book "at the very last minute" after discussing it with his girlfriend Lou Teasdale.

A friend of his former partner, who was away at the time, was set to stay over after coming to his home to watch a boxing match.

Carroll says the incident occurred while he was sleeping and he then threw the man out of the house, before knocking him unconscious as he tried to return.

Carroll, who also played in the Premier League for Liverpool and West Ham, called the police and was "sobbing" in the arms of his children's nanny.

The unnamed attacker was found guilty of sexual offences and placed on the sex offender register. Carroll testified in court, a process he says was "humiliating and embarrassing and absolutely horrendous".

Carroll wrote: "I was sexually assaulted, there I said it. Scary to even think about and only a few people knew about it before now.

"Me and Lou spent a lot of time discussing whether to mention it in this book or not. I avoided my publisher for so long that they probably suspected I got cold feet.

"Scary to talk about but it's made [me] the person I am today as much as any of the good stuff. And if me talking about it helps just one person then good, it will have been worth it."

Carroll, who won nine England caps, added: "What happened to me affected every facet of my life. I'd think about it every day, making it difficult to focus on anything else, including footballâ¦ The trauma of what happened to me hasn't gone away."

Carroll joined Dagenham in July 2025 and has made six appearances in the National League South this season.

News.title: Firm fined £1m after man killed by window that fell from luxury penthouse
News.content:
Ferris said her husband's death was "so sudden" and "out of the blue".

In a statement read out in court, she said: "If somebody had done something differently â anything â it would have changed our lives. We wouldn't be in this position.

"I know it wasn't just one person, but one person could have changed this.

"What those companies did killed my husband.

"The thought this could have happened to anybody is always with me. It could have been a child."

She also told the court that 400 people attended her husband's funeral, and said "he is missed by so many it was unbelievable".

At the time of the incident, television host and fellow West Ham fan James Corden paid tribute to Mick Ferris on Twitter, saying: "He was a huge West Ham fan and has passed away in the most sudden of circumstances."

He added: "Tell your loved ones you love them today."

HSE principal inspector James Goldfinch said: "The fact lessons had not been learnt from a near miss the year before makes what happened on that day all the more galling.

"For a window to fall once was quite extraordinary, for it to fall again was simply criminal."
